senses.definition: the ability to make good judgments and quick decisions, typically in a particular domain
senses.example: Her business acumen turned a small shop into a chain.

senses.definition: ridiculously old-fashioned
senses.example: His antediluvian views on women shocked the younger staff.

senses.definition: harshness of tone or manner
senses.example: "That will do," she said with some asperity.

senses.definition: kind and friendly toward a younger or less experienced person
senses.example: The avuncular coach always had time for new players.

senses.definition: in a state of pitiful or contemptible intellectual or moral ignorance
senses.example: The missionaries saw the islanders as benighted, which said more about them.

senses.definition: an unfounded rumor or story
senses.example: The claim that the senator was a spy is an old canard.

senses.definition: tending to find fault or raise petty objections
senses.example: The captious reviewer complained about the font.

senses.definition: to make petty or unnecessary objections
senses.example: They caviled at the cost of the coffee but approved the budget.

senses.definition: a trivial and annoying objection
senses.example: The editor dismissed the reader's cavils.

senses.definition: willing to please others; obliging to an excessive degree
senses.example: The complaisant host agreed to every request.

senses.definition: to admit as acceptable or possible; to tolerate
senses.example: The school will not countenance bullying.

senses.definition: a person's face or facial expression
senses.example: His countenance darkened when he heard the news.

senses.definition: contemptibly lacking in courage; cowardly
senses.example: The craven guard fled at the first sign of trouble.

senses.definition: in keeping with good taste and propriety; polite and restrained
senses.example: The guests at the embassy dinner were decorous and quiet.

senses.definition: to catch sight of
senses.example: From the tower we could descry a ship on the horizon.

senses.definition: lacking a plan, purpose or enthusiasm
senses.example: They made a few desultory attempts to clean the house.

senses.definition: to give the right to vote to
senses.example: The amendment enfranchised women in 1920.

senses.definition: extremely delicate and light in a way that seems too perfect for this world
senses.example: Her ethereal voice filled the cathedral.

senses.definition: to deprive of vital or essential content
senses.example: The amendments eviscerated the original bill.

senses.definition: to disembowel a person or animal
senses.example: The hunter eviscerated the deer before carrying it home.

senses.definition: to show or declare that someone is not guilty of wrongdoing
senses.example: The new evidence exculpated the prisoner.

senses.definition: critical explanation or interpretation of a text, especially of scripture
senses.example: The scholar wrote a detailed exegesis of the poem.

senses.definition: a tedious moralizing lecture or discourse
senses.example: He gave us a homily about the value of hard work.

senses.definition: unable to be upset or excited; calm
senses.example: The imperturbable pilot landed the damaged plane.

senses.definition: to bring oneself into favor with someone by flattering or trying to please them
senses.example: He tried to ingratiate himself with the new boss.

senses.definition: accustomed to something, especially something unpleasant
senses.example: Years in the city had inured her to the noise.

senses.definition: to criticize someone or something harshly
senses.example: The coach lambasted the referee after the game.

senses.definition: a tedious recital or repetitive series
senses.example: He listened to a litany of complaints about the service.

senses.definition: a series of petitions for use in church services
senses.example: The priest led the congregation in the litany.

senses.definition: a plot or scheme
senses.example: The novel follows the machinations of a scheming duke.

senses.definition: a person's look or manner, especially one of a particular kind indicating their character or mood
senses.example: He has the serious mien of a judge.

senses.definition: a sudden attack or violent expression of a particular emotion or activity
senses.example: The joke sent him into paroxysms of laughter.

senses.definition: of or like a portent
senses.example: The portentous silence before the storm frightened the children.

senses.definition: done in a pompously or overly solemn manner so as to impress
senses.example: The narrator's portentous voice made the documentary feel like a sermon.

senses.definition: generally considered or reputed to be
senses.example: The putative father of the child denied the claim.

senses.definition: to make a statement or assertion less absolute; to add reservations to
senses.example: She qualified her praise by noting a few weaknesses.

senses.definition: to be entitled to a particular benefit or privilege by fulfilling a necessary condition
senses.example: Students qualify for a discount on train tickets.

words.note: To qualify a statement is to limit or soften it.

senses.definition: a person who tells anecdotes in a skillful and amusing way
senses.example: A gifted raconteur, he kept the dinner guests laughing.

senses.definition: distant from the lives and concerns of ordinary people; esoteric
senses.example: The rarefied world of high fashion bewildered her.

senses.definition: (of air, especially that at high altitudes) of lower pressure than usual; thin
senses.example: Climbers struggle to breathe in the rarefied air.

senses.definition: the tendency of a convicted criminal to reoffend
senses.example: Education programs in prisons can reduce recidivism.

senses.definition: (of a subject or knowledge) little known; abstruse
senses.example: The book is full of recondite references to medieval law.

senses.definition: referring to sexual matters in an amusingly rude or irreverent way
senses.example: The sailors sang ribald songs.

senses.definition: a person's nickname
senses.example: He earned the sobriquet "the Iron Chancellor."

senses.definition: sleepy; drowsy
senses.example: The heat made the audience somnolent.

senses.definition: causing or suggestive of sleep
senses.example: The somnolent hum of bees filled the garden.

senses.definition: to supply an ungenerous or inadequate amount of something
senses.example: Don't stint on the butter.

senses.definition: a person's fixed or allotted period of work
senses.example: She did a two-year stint in the navy.

senses.definition: to act as a neutralizing or counterbalancing force to something
senses.example: She tempered her criticism with praise.

senses.definition: to improve the hardness and elasticity of steel or other metal by heating and then cooling it
senses.example: The blacksmith tempered the sword blade.

words.note: As a verb, temper means to moderate or soften.

senses.definition: shaking or quivering slightly
senses.example: She spoke in a tremulous voice.

senses.definition: timid; nervous
senses.example: He gave a tremulous smile as he walked on stage.

senses.definition: a beginner or novice
senses.example: The course is ideal for tyros who have never painted.

senses.definition: offense or annoyance
senses.example: She took umbrage at his remarks about her cooking.

senses.definition: unexpected and inappropriate or adverse
senses.example: The guard noticed nothing untoward.

senses.definition: the appearance of being true or real
senses.example: The novel's rich detail gives it verisimilitude.

senses.definition: a change of circumstances or fortune, typically one that is unwelcome or unpleasant
senses.example: The firm survived the vicissitudes of the market.

senses.definition: (of a cruel or violent action) deliberate and unprovoked
senses.example: The wanton destruction of the forest angered the villagers.

senses.definition: sexually immodest or promiscuous
senses.example: The play's wanton heroine scandalized audiences.

senses.definition: attractive or appealing in appearance or character
senses.example: The puppy had a winsome face.

senses.definition: one's customary behavior in a particular situation
senses.example: She rose early, as was her wont.

senses.definition: accustomed; apt
senses.example: He was wont to sing in the shower.

senses.definition: a person who is fanatical and uncompromising in pursuit of their religious, political or other ideals
senses.example: The zealots refused any compromise.
